coeus.reasoning: Model projection (272.9) sits almost exactly on FanDuel's line (272.5) with only a 0.4-yard edge, so there's no real statistical lean. Recent totals swing widely (148 to 339) and while WAS ranks bottom-10 against the combined category (287.6 allowed/g), Purdy's own 5-game average (264.8) is already below the line, offsetting the plus matchup. Too thin an edge to pick a side.

WAS ranks top-10 against the run (rank 6, 73.6 allowed/g) and mid-tier against receiving backs, and CMC's vs-tier average (83.0 expected) reinforces the lower number. San Francisco being a 7.5-point home favorite with a 29.5 implied total doesn't change the recent usage pattern enough to flip this.

coeus.reasoning: Model projection (201.7) is well below the 254.5 line (20.7% gap, flagged CHECK), but the underlying matchup data backs the lower number: SF ranks top-10 against QB passing (rank 8, 210.8 allowed/g) and is elite against QB rushing (rank 2, just 6.6 allowed/g), which directly suppresses Daniels' usual rushing upside (weighted avg 56.9 cut to a 45.1 projection). Washington is a 7.5-point road underdog with only a 22.0 implied team total, a negative script that typically limits called runs even if it bumps pass attempts, and his last meeting vs a similar top defense level produced modest marks. The data supports the model's lean despite the large gap, so UNDER is the call, though the CHECK flag keeps confidence short of max.
